colors.description: The one loud color: something waits for your decision (waiting badge, needs-you dots). The theme's info blue, never the error red or the brand orange.
Text on the decision color: the page color (dark on the dark themes' light blue, white on the light themes' deep blue).
Claude's hue, for its mark and puck (oklch .8 .09 55 dark, .5 .12 50 light).
Codex's hue, for its mark and puck (oklch .83 .08 180 dark, .5 .09 180 light).
Gemini's hue, for its mark and puck (oklch .79 .09 275 dark, .5 .14 275 light).
Background of the lines an agent is working on after Edit with Agent.

friedliver.discuss.maxRounds.markdownDescription: Rounds a `/discuss` runs at most before it is summed up. It ends sooner when everyone agrees.

enumDescriptions: A board with a column for each position and each agent under the one it holds, then a meter showing how sure each agent is and how far it moved.
Only the board: a column for each position, each agent under the one it holds.
Only the meter: each agent on a line between the two positions, nearer the end it is surer of.
A timeline: each round in order, with each agent's turn and whose point it answers.
friedliver.discuss.layout.markdownDescription: How a `/discuss` card shows the discussion while it runs. Once it ends, every layout shows the same conclusion; open cards change as soon as you change this.

friedliver.discuss.tokenBudget.markdownDescription: Tokens (estimated, sent and received) a `/discuss` may use; past it the discussion stops and is summed up.

friedliver.chat.autoAllowLinkedReads.markdownDescription: Lets an agent read the chat that handed it its task, or that consulted it, without asking each time. Off by default: reading another chat waits for your OK. Read from your user settings only.

friedliver.welcome.onEmptyWindow.markdownDescription: Open the FriedLiver Welcome page (live agents, recent folders, an Ask box) in a window with no folder.

friedliver.chat.fontFamily.markdownDescription: Font for the chat, the Agent Manager and the other FriedLiver views. Empty uses the editor's chat font (the system font). Takes effect when a view next opens.

friedliver.chat.fontSize.markdownDescription: Text size (px) a new chat tab starts at. In a tab, Cmd/Ctrl + `=` / `-` / `0` changes that tab only. Takes effect when a view next opens.

friedliver.chat.accentColor.markdownDescription: The chat's one accent colour, used only as the border of the recommended answer. Leave it empty to use the theme's button colour. Takes effect when a view next opens.

friedliver.remote.enabled.markdownDescription: Lets phones you pair control your agents from the same Wi-Fi (FriedLiver Remote). Off by default; **FriedLiver: Remote Control…** starts it and shows the pairing QR code. Only your own user settings can turn it on, never a workspace's.

friedliver.remote.tailscale.markdownDescription: Also listen on this Mac's Tailscale address, so paired phones on your tailnet reach FriedLiver Remote from anywhere. Never the public internet, never a relay. See docs/REMOTE.md.

friedliver.voice.language.markdownDescription: Language the composer's mic (macOS) listens for, as a BCP-47 tag such as `en-IN` or `hi-IN`. `auto` uses the system language.

friedliver.voice.silenceSeconds.description: The composer's mic stops after this many seconds without new words. It always stops after 60 seconds.

friedliver.agents.claude.command.description: Program that runs Claude over ACP. Changing it restarts Claude. Read from user settings only, never from a workspace.

friedliver.agents.codex.command.description: Program that runs Codex over ACP. Changing it restarts Codex. Read from user settings only, never from a workspace.

friedliver.agents.gemini.command.description: Program that runs Gemini over ACP. Changing it restarts Gemini. Read from user settings only, never from a workspace.

friedliver.agents.antigravity.command.description: Google's Antigravity CLI (agy). It has no ACP mode, so FriedLiver runs it through its own adapter. Changing it restarts Antigravity. Read from user settings only, never from a workspace.

friedliver.agents.antigravity.args.description: Extra arguments for each agy call (e.g. --project). FriedLiver sets the mode, model, effort and permissions itself and drops flags that would change them.

friedliver.agents.copilot.command.description: Program that runs GitHub Copilot CLI over ACP. Changing it restarts Copilot. Read from user settings only, never from a workspace.

friedliver.agents.copilot.args.description: Arguments for the Copilot program (e.g. --effort=high, which Copilot fixes for the whole server).

friedliver.agents.opencode.command.description: Program that runs OpenCode over ACP. Changing it restarts OpenCode. Read from user settings only, never from a workspace.

friedliver.agents.custom.markdownDescription: More agents: any program that speaks ACP on stdin/stdout. Each shows up like the built-in ones (pickers, `@id`, Agents & Accounts, models, approvals, `/discuss`). Read from user settings only, never from a workspace. Put API keys in your shell environment rather than here.

id.description: What @ mentions it: lower-case letters and digits, not a built-in agent's name.

name.description: The name shown for it. Default: the id.

command.description: The program that speaks ACP, e.g. opencode.

install.description: The command that installs it, shown on its Accounts card.

signIn.description: How to sign in, shown on its Accounts card.

enumDescriptions: Web links you click open in a tab of FriedLiver's browser, on the right. Hold Cmd/Ctrl in a chat to use the system browser.
Web links open in your system browser. Hold Cmd/Ctrl in a chat to use FriedLiver's browser.
friedliver.links.openIn.markdownDescription: Where web links you click open: in a chat, the Agent Manager and Images, and (through the editor's link openers) in Markdown previews, hovers, the editor and the terminal. Per-site choices you made in `#workbench.externalUriOpeners#` still win.

friedliver.maxRunningAgents.description: How many agent processes may run at once. The least recently used idle one stops first.

enumDescriptions: 30 seconds after start and every 4 hours, ask GitHub whether a newer FriedLiver release is out, and offer to install it.
friedliver.update.mode.description: In the FriedLiver app, check GitHub for newer releases and offer to install them. Sends nothing but that request.

friedliver.idleStopMinutes.description: Stop an agent after this many minutes without a turn, to free its memory. 0 keeps agents running.

enumDescriptions: Agents can list agents and chats. Asking another agent, messaging a chat or reading one waits for your OK.
Agents can ask other agents, message chats and read them without asking you each time.
Agents get no FriedLiver tools and can't reach other agents or chats.
friedliver.connections.agentToAgent.description: Whether agents can reach other agents and chats through FriedLiver's tools. Applies to agent sessions started after the change.

enumDescriptions: Edits and commands wait for you.
Edits go through without asking (each turn can be undone); commands wait for you.
friedliver.approvals.default.description: The approval level new chats start at. Full auto is chosen per chat, never here. Read from user settings only, so a repository can't make agents run without asking.

friedliver.approvals.autoRoutineSeconds.markdownDescription: Routine requests (reads, `git status`, the project's tests, lint and build) allow themselves once after this many seconds, with a visible countdown you can stop (Esc). 0 turns it off. Review and careful requests always wait for you. Read from user settings only.

friedliver.approvals.fullAutoGuards.markdownDescription: Full auto's hard limits. On: even on Full auto (or an "Always allow" rule) FriedLiver asks before a browser action that takes a chat from a page on the internet onto this computer or its network (localhost, private and link-local addresses, judged by what the name resolves to), before every download an agent starts, before a command that runs a file the chat downloaded or wrote in its last 3 turns, before package installs, and before piping a download into a shell. Read from your user settings only: a workspace can't turn it off.

friedliver.notify.decisions.description: Show a notification with buttons when an agent waits for you and its chat isn't on screen or the window isn't focused.

friedliver.companion.enabled.description: When an agent in any chat waits for you (a permission, a command, an edit to review, a question), a character runs in along the bottom of the window to the middle and asks in a card beside it, with the answer buttons. Careful requests and plans are answered in the chat.

friedliver.companion.characters.markdownDescription:
The character each agent sends, by agent id. A value is a built-in name (`jas`, `bolt`, `owl`, `thunder`, `fox`, `panda`, `smash`, `skip`), a local file of your own, or `{ "idle": file, "run": file }` with a run-in too (one file is used for both). Pictures: `.svg`, `.png`, `.gif`, `.webp` up to 5 MB. Short videos: `.webm`, `.mp4`, `.m4v`, `.mov` up to 20 MB, played muted and looping; FriedLiver can't decode H.264/HEVC, so prefer `.webm` (VP9, with alpha for a cut-out). Paths are absolute or start with `~`; no web addresses. A clip or picture with transparency or a flat-coloured background floats (the colour is keyed out); a busy background sits in a rounded frame. Anything that doesn't load or play falls back to the built-in character. Read from your user settings only.

Example: `{ "claude": "~/Pictures/cat.png", "codex": "~/FriedLiverCharacters/codex.webm", "gemini": { "idle": "~/Pictures/owl.webp", "run": "~/Pictures/owl-run.gif" } }`

friedliver.companion.folder.markdownDescription:
A folder of your own characters, checked after your `characters` entries and before the repository: `<folder>/<agent id>` with `.svg`, `.png`, `.gif`, `.webp` (up to 5 MB) or `.webm`, `.mp4`, `.m4v`, `.mov` (up to 20 MB; `.webm` VP9 plays best), and `<agent id>-run.*` for the run-in. Read from your user settings only.

Example: `~/FriedLiverCharacters` holding `codex.webm`, `claude.png` and `claude-run.gif`.

friedliver.companion.repo.markdownDescription:
A git repository of your own characters, so they follow you to every machine. FriedLiver keeps a shallow clone and pulls it at startup, every 6 hours and on **FriedLiver: Update Characters**. Its root holds `<agent id>.*` and `<agent id>-run.*`, the same files and limits as the folder setting. A private repository works through your existing git sign-in (credential helper, `gh auth`, or ssh key); FriedLiver never asks for or stores a token. Only `https://`, `ssh://` and `git@` addresses. Order: your `characters` entry, then the folder, then this repository, then the built-in character. Read from your user settings only.

Example: `https://github.com/MrArun005/friedliver-characters`

friedliver.notify.finished.description: Show a notification when an agent finishes a task and its chat isn't on screen or the window isn't focused.

friedliver.claudeSessions.showAll.description: Show every outside Claude Code session: keep greeting-only ones and don't move sessions idle for over a week to Archived.

friedliver.showClaudeCodeSessions.description: Show this folder's Claude Code sessions started outside FriedLiver (the claude CLI, the Claude Code extension) in the Agent Manager, read from ~/.claude/projects. FriedLiver only reads them.

friedliver.images.storageLimitMB.markdownDescription: How much space FriedLiver's copies of the images agents read, take and make may use, in MB. Past it, the oldest unpinned copies are removed. Pinned images are always kept.

friedliver.images.keepDays.markdownDescription: Unpinned image copies, and FriedLiver's own screenshots, older than this many days are removed. **Done looking** in the Images view removes them sooner.

friedliver.restoreChats.description: Bring this folder's chats back when the window opens again. They are kept in the editor's storage for the folder, without images, API keys or tokens. Turning this off deletes the saved chats.

friedliver.edit.defaultAgent.description: The agent Edit with Agent uses in a folder until you pick another there (start the request with @claude, @codex, @gemini or @antigravity). Read from user settings only, so a repository can't choose where your code goes.

friedliver.browser.externalClients.markdownDescription: Opt-in: lets Claude Code (the VS Code extension, or `claude` in a terminal) use FriedLiver's browser tools only, through a stdio MCP server named `friedliver-browser` that FriedLiver adds to `~/.claude.json` (no secret in it; it reads a token that changes every launch from FriedLiver's storage). Off by default: FriedLiver writes nothing to `~/.claude.json` until you turn this on or run **FriedLiver: Connect Claude Code to the browser**; turning it off removes the entry FriedLiver added. Every action still asks you first. Read from your user settings only.

friedliver.browser.externalAutoApprove.markdownDescription: Lets Claude Code act in FriedLiver's browser (open, click, type, back, reload) without asking each time. Off by default; Full auto in a FriedLiver chat does not cover it. Read from your user settings only.

friedliver.browser.downloadFolder.markdownDescription: Where FriedLiver's browser saves downloads. `~` is your home folder; empty means your system's Downloads folder. A file never replaces another: a second `report.pdf` is saved as `report (1).pdf`. Nothing downloaded is opened or run by itself, and files keep the system's downloaded-from-the-internet mark (macOS quarantine, Windows Mark of the Web). Read from your user settings only.

friedliver.browser.downloadAsk.markdownDescription: Ask where to save each download you start in FriedLiver's browser, instead of saving it to `#friedliver.browser.downloadFolder#`. Downloads an agent starts are always saved to that folder, after you allow them. Read from your user settings only.

friedliver.browser.relaxLocalhostCors.markdownDescription: Adds permissive CORS response headers (the requesting origin, credentials allowed, and a 204 answer to preflights) to responses from `http://localhost`, `127.0.0.1` and `[::1]` in FriedLiver's browser only. Nothing else changes: other sites keep normal CORS and web security. Read from your user settings only.

friedliver.usage.dailyTokenWarning.markdownDescription: Warns once a day when the tokens the agents report for today, across the chats in a window, pass this many. Counted on this computer only; nothing is sent anywhere. `0` (the default) turns it off.

friedliver.system.enabled.markdownDescription: Let agents ask to act on your Mac or Windows PC through the `system_*` tools: open apps, files and links, bring apps to the front, use the clipboard, show notifications, change the volume, run Shortcuts and screenshot a window. Each action asks you first and is logged in **FriedLiver: System Actions**. Not available on Linux. See docs/SYSTEM-CONTROL.md.

friedliver.system.fullAutoAllowed.markdownDescription: Let chats on Full auto use the `system_*` tools without asking. Off: they still ask. Reading the clipboard, window screenshots and terminal-like apps ask every time either way. Only your user settings count.

friedliver.system.tools.markdownDescription: Turn single `system_*` tools on or off.

system_focus.description: Bring an app to the front

friedliver.inlineEdit.agent.description: The agent Inline Edit (Ctrl/Cmd+I) asks. It only proposes text; FriedLiver changes the file when you accept. Rebind the shortcut in Keyboard Shortcuts under FriedLiver: Inline Edit.

friedliver.index.enabled.markdownDescription: Keep a local index of the workspace (file list, definitions, imports, keywords) that agents query with the `index_*` tools to find code faster. Nothing leaves the machine. Skips untrusted folders, `.gitignore`d and `files.exclude`d files, binaries, files over 1 MB, and secret-looking files (`.env*`, `*.pem`, `*.key`, `id_rsa*`).

friedliver.index.maxFiles.markdownDescription: Most files the project index holds per workspace folder.

friedliver.index.maxMemoryMB.markdownDescription: Roughly how much memory (MB) the project index may use per workspace folder before it stops adding files. A stopped index shows *Partial index* in the status bar; raise this to index a large repository in full (about 400 for 80,000 files, at roughly 1 GB of memory).

friedliver.index.primer.markdownDescription: Start each new chat with a compact project map from the index: top-level folders with file counts and the files most likely relevant to the first message (at most 1,500 tokens, sharing the shared rules' 8 KB cap). Saves the agent exploring to find its way.

walkthroughs.title: Get Started with Agents
walkthroughs.description: Agents propose, you decide. Pick how much an agent may do on its own; edits show as diffs, commands wait for you, and every turn can be undone.

steps.title: Open a folder
steps.description:
Agents read, write and run commands only inside the folder you open.
[Open Folder](command:workbench.action.files.openFolder)

media.altText: A FriedLiver window with a folder open in the Explorer.

steps.title: Sign in to Claude, Codex or Gemini
steps.description:
**Agents & Accounts** has a card per agent: install it, sign in with its own login (Google, ChatGPT, Claude) or an API key kept in the editor's secret storage (Gemini also takes Vertex AI), see which account is in use, sign out, and pick the model and effort new chats start with. Your logins stay with the company that runs each agent. Prefer another agent extension, such as Claude Code or Cline? Get it from the gallery as it is.
[Open Agents & Accounts](command:friedliver.accounts)
[Get Another Agent Extension](command:friedliver.otherAgents)

media.altText: The Agents accounts list: one agent signed in, one not installed, one waiting for sign-in.

steps.title: Run a task on several agents
steps.description:
The Agent Manager sends one task to several agents at once and sorts their work into Needs you, Working and Done.
[Open the Agent Manager](command:friedliver.openTasks)

media.altText: The Agent Manager board with one task sent to three agents.

steps.title: Ask another agent with @gemini
steps.description:
In any chat, start a message with **@gemini**, **@claude** or **@codex** to ask that agent. Its answer comes back to the same chat, so a second agent can review the first one's work.
[Open a Chat](command:friedliver.newChat)

media.altText: A chat where a message starting with @gemini gets an answer from Gemini in the same chat.

steps.title: Edit code where it is
steps.description:
Select code and press **Ctrl/Cmd+I** for an inline edit: describe the change, watch the proposal as a diff, then accept (Ctrl/Cmd+Enter) or reject (Esc). Right-click **Edit with Agent** lets the agent edit the file itself, as a diff you review. Right-click also has **Ask About Selection**, and Source Control has **Review My Changes**.
[Edit with Agent](command:friedliver.editSelection)

media.altText: Lines selected in format.ts, the Edit with Claude box asking for the change, and the status bar saying Claude is editing format.ts.
